\label{lemma:obvious_on_mimima}
    Let functions $f_1, \ldots, f_k$ be continuous having
    unique strict minimum, $f_i:\mathbb{R^{p} \rightarrow \mathbb{R^{1}$, and let $h(x) =
    \min\{f_1(x),\ldots,f_k(x)\}$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R^{p}$. Define a set
    $S = \{x \in \mathbb{R^{p}\,|\,f_1(x) = \cdots = f_k(x) \}$.
    If $h$ has a local minimum at $x_0 \in S$, then $f_i$ has the
    strict global minimum at $x_0$ for all $i = 1, \ldots, k$.

    If $h$ has a local minimum at $x_0 \in S$, then there exists a
    neighbourhood $U_{(x_0)}$ of $x_0$ such that
    $$
        (\forall x \in U_{(x_0)})(h(x) \geq h(x_0) = f_1(x_0) \cdots =

    $x_0$ has to be also the point of the global
    minima of the functions $f_i, i = 1, \ldots, k$.

\proofend

smallest residuum at $\beta$.
